chapter_name: Introduction to Prescribed Ragas (Nirdharit Ragon Ka Parichay)
learning_objective: 🎼 Master the classical profiles, key notes, and singing times of the syllabus's main Ragas—Bihag, Bhairav, Kafi, and Yaman!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: Raga Introduction (Details including Thaat, Vadi, Samvadi, Time, Jati, and Aroha-Avaroha)
A Raga of Kalyan Thaat that uses only the Teevra 'Ma' (Sung in the first quarter of the night)
A solemn morning Raga of Bhairav Thaat where 'Re' and 'Dha' are Komal (flat)
A midnight Raga of Kafi Thaat where 'Ga' and 'Ni' are Komal (flat)
A night Raga of Bilawal Thaat that distinctly uses both the Shuddh and Teevra 'Ma'

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Thaat: Kalyan | Vadi: Ga, Samvadi: Ni | Jati: Sampoorna-Sampoorna | Time: First quarter of the night. It uses the Teevra Madhyam (m॑), all other notes are pure. In the ascent (Aroha), 'Sa' and 'Pa' are often skipped or lightly touched (Ni Re Ga m॑ Dha Ni Sa').

Thaat: Bhairav | Vadi: Dha, Samvadi: Re | Jati: Sampoorna-Sampoorna | Time: Morning (Sandhiprakash Raga). It uses Komal 'Re' and 'Dha' (rॆ, d॒). It is an incredibly solemn Raga, deeply associated with devotion (Bhakti Ras).

Thaat: Kafi | Vadi: Pa, Samvadi: Sa | Jati: Sampoorna-Sampoorna | Time: Midnight. It uses Komal 'Ga' and 'Ni' (g॒, n॒). It is highly popular for lighter classical forms like Thumri, Tappa, and Hori due to its romantic (Shringar) essence.

Thaat: Bilawal | Vadi: Ga, Samvadi: Ni | Jati: Audav-Sampoorna | Time: Second quarter of the night. Its Aroha skips 'Re' and 'Dha'. Its unique feature is the use of both the pure 'Ma' (mostly) and the sharp Teevra 'Ma' (m॑) to enhance beauty.
The key to recognizing them: Yaman uses Teevra 'm॑', Bhairav uses Komal 'rॆ d॒', Kafi uses Komal 'g॒ n॒', and Bihag uses both forms of 'Ma'.

fun_activity.title: 🎵 The Raga Detective
fun_activity.instructions: If you wake up early in the morning and hear someone singing 'Sa rॆ Ga Ma Pa d॒ Ni Sa'' (where Re and Dha sound flat and heavy), you immediately know they are singing the morning Raga, Bhairav!

exam_tips: 📌 Expect a full descriptive question on at least one Raga. Create a table memorizing the Thaat, Vadi, Samvadi, Jati, Time, Aroha, Avaroha, and Pakad for each.
📌 Note the careful usage of the two 'Ma's in Raga Bihag versus the single Teevra 'Ma' in Raga Yaman.
📌 What is a 'Sandhiprakash Raga'? Answer: Ragas sung during twilight/dusk/dawn when day and night meet (e.g., Raga Bhairav).
quick_recap: ⭐ Raga Yaman is also widely known by the name 'Kalyan'.
⭐ Raga Bhairav is a classic 'Sandhiprakash' (twilight) Raga sung at dawn.
⭐ Raga Bihag belongs to the 'Audav-Sampoorna' Jati, meaning it uses 5 notes ascending and 7 descending.
